summary: Axod starts and observes a Pi process over a bounded local bridge, accepting events only after authentication and exact pane identity binding; takeover preserves active work unless the user explicitly requests restart.
trigger: Axod launches an agent pane, follows the current Pi process, or takes over its transcript for restart/recovery.

steps.action: Acquire the per-transcript exclusive writer lock, construct a short absolute Unix socket path and launch the configured Pi command with Axo-managed session flags, extension path and scoped bridge credentials.
The Pi extension listens on the Unix socket and authenticates Axod using the protocol version and session bridge token.

Axod verifies the bridge hello matches the exact session UUID, pane ID, transcript path, initial working directory and launched process ID; then it accepts one strictly increasing, bounded event stream and reports activity/resume events.
For ordinary recovery request idle shutdown and wait for lock release; explicit restart may request shutdown, verify the Pi process group, then escalate TERM/KILL within bounded waits.
The inherited writer lock proves Pi liveness; after release Axod reacquires it and may reopen only the original Axo-owned transcript.
